behavior_change: In the next run, the only observable changes are that the agent opens by reading its own log and that its ledger line contains the substring 'taste rule' or 'archetype' plus the word 'queue'; every other duty these two files add (the four accuracy channels, the repairs[] rows, the queue drain, the heat and scenario boundary as a mutation rule, the two-occurrence hardening bar) produces no observable a future run can be checked against, because no gate reads it and the calibrators explicitly preserve those fields verbatim instead of computing them.
checks_touched: tools/check_radar.py:main ran_today guard (unchanged by the diff; the contract claims coverage this branch does not give on a zero-card run)
tools/check_radar.py:check 5 calibration freshness (counts HARDENED rules, never compares occurrences to origin)
tools/check_radar.py:check 7 ledger regex taste[- ]?(ledger|rule) and (click )?queue (substring, not count)
tools/check_chain.py:check 9 preservation (tests heat/scenario DISAPPEARANCE only, never mutation)
tools/check_chain.py:check 10 LEDGER_RULE_GATE = 2026-08-30 (inert on 2026-08-29, the day both contracts assert it)

cost_if_wrong: Six weeks out the failure is silent and cumulative. The radar records a run of clean weekday sweeps whose zero-card days were never gated at all, so a scanner that has quietly stopped searching is indistinguishable from a scanner finding nothing. A chain re-run 'corrects' a crowdedness score to fit its new structure, the verdict is rewritten to stay consistent, validate.py and check_chain.py both pass, and the money corner moves under an analyst who never re-scored it. Taste rules keep hardening off single observations because the contract's stated bar and the store's actual bar disagree, so the filter that decides what Upstream is allowed to look at tightens on evidence that was never required to repeat. None of the three leaves a mark in the ledger, and all three read downstream as the world getting harder.
how_you_would_know: Two of the three would show, late. A heat mutation is visible only by diffing a chain file's heat blocks against an earlier commit by hand, or in map_calibrate's verdict_mismatches if the rewriter was sloppy enough to leave the verdict inconsistent, which is exactly the case that already fails. A single-occurrence HARDENED rule is visible by reading scout-log proposed_rules and comparing origin to occurrences, which no script does. The zero-card radar failure is the one where the honest answer is that nothing would show it: check_radar exits 0 with NOT RUN TODAY, radar-gate.py never fires because no signal file was written, and the only remaining detector, p_radar_sentinel in the weekly smoke job, has by nell-scanner.md's own admission never fired. A duty whose sole detector has never run once is not monitored, and by the contract's own rule that is a REJECT-level finding on that clause.

challenges.claim: check_radar.py is Nell's postlude gate, so the radar contract's duties are machine-checked (nell-scanner.md, Scripts I run, and CLAUDE.md's radar row: 'All of this is machine-checked by tools/check_radar.py').
challenges.attack: The gate disables itself on precisely the run that most needs it. ran_today = bool(touched or radar_lines): a sweep that writes no signal card and no RADAR ledger line exits 0 printing NOT RUN TODAY, and every check is skipped. The contract explicitly permits zero cards ('0 to 5 new or updated signal cards', 'Nothing cleared the bar is a valid, first-class output'), so the unguarded case is the routine case for a weekday routine, not an edge case. The Stop hook does not close it either: radar-gate.py returns allow() unless the transcript shows a write under data/signals/, which a zero-card run does not have. The contract's answer to this is the prose rule 'a silent no-op is the only wrong result, write RADAR-DEGRADED', which is a promise, and promises regress. The gate cannot fail on a lazy run, so it certifies laziness.

challenges.claim: Atlas is walled off from the analyst's work: 'Stores I own and write: data/chains/<slug>.json except links[].heat, heat_as_of, scenarios[] and scenarios_as_of', backed by check_chain's preservation check.
challenges.attack: Preservation tests disappearance, not mutation. check_chain check 9 computes lost_heat as links whose HEAD version had heat and whose current version does not, and gone as prior scenario ids absent now. A link whose crowdedness score is rewritten from 35 to 75 still has a heat block and its scenario ids are all still present, so the check reports a clean preservation line. validate.py does not catch it either: v_chain only recomputes verdict and money_corner from the scores that are there (band_for), so a mutated score with a correspondingly mutated verdict is internally consistent and validates. The realistic hazard of a re-run is not a rebuild that drops heat, which the file itself calls out and therefore guards against; it is a rebuild that tidies a stale score to fit the new structure. That path is guarded by one word, 'except', with no exit code behind it, and the contract presents the gate as though it covered the boundary it names.

challenges.claim: Nell and Atlas have real, separated lanes, and each contract's 'What I do not do' section describes an enforced boundary.
challenges.attack: Every store either agent writes is DATA tier, so collab-gate.py and check_collab.py are indifferent to which of them writes what; the lane is prose in both directions. Worse than unenforced, it is mis-enforced in one place. atlas-cartographer.md requires Atlas to write 'the chained signal's status and chain_id', and check_chain check 7 fails the run if he does not. That write lands in data/signals/<id>.json, which radar-gate.py treats as proof that the session did radar work: verified directly, from_tool_use('Edit', {'file_path': 'data/signals/SIG-20260829-03.json'}) returns that path and the hook's regex matches it. A pure chain run therefore hits a Stop hook demanding a RADAR ledger line dated today and a scout-log calibration regenerated today. The cheapest way past a blocking hook is to satisfy it, so the gate's incentive is for a chain session to write a RADAR line it did not earn and to run another agent's calibrator. A hook that pressures a false ledger entry is worse than an absent hook, because the ledger is what every later audit reads.

challenges.claim: nell-scanner.md Channel 1: 'Nothing hardens from a single note. The same pattern appearing a second time promotes it to HARDENED and writes it into data/taste.md with both quotes and both dates.'
challenges.attack: The store this clause governs already contradicts it, on the day both landed. data/radar/scout-log.json holds TASTE-001 and TASTE-002, both status HARDENED, both occurrences 1, both hardened_at 2026-08-29, each citing a single ledger quote. They are not defective rows: data/taste.md, which Nell also owns and writes, states a two-origin bar under which METHOD-origin rules harden on first application and only PREFERENCE-origin rules need two occurrences. So the contract states as absolute a rule its own store applies conditionally, and the live rules are either illegitimate or the sentence is wrong. That this is drift and not a considered choice is settled by the sibling file: atlas-cartographer.md states the same two-origin bar correctly ('METHOD-origin archetypes harden on first application with cited evidence; PREFERENCE-origin ones need two occurrences'). Nothing can catch the discrepancy: check_radar's check 5 counts rules whose status is HARDENED and never reads origin or occurrences, and scout_calibrate.py preserves proposed_rules verbatim. The clause that decides what the machine is allowed to stop looking at is the one clause with no arbiter.

challenges.claim: Both contracts present their accuracy loops as measured, not remembered: 'Four channels, recomputed every run into data/radar/scout-log.json' and 'Recomputed every run into data/chains/_map-log.json by tools/map_calibrate.py'.
challenges.attack: The scripts say the opposite in their own docstrings. scout_calibrate.py: 'Judgment fields (proposed_rules, spot_tests, repairs, notes) are the agent's to write and are preserved verbatim across runs.' map_calibrate.py: 'Judgment fields (archetypes, spot_tests, repairs, notes) belong to the agent and are preserved verbatim.' So Nell's Channel 1 (notes swept since last run, PROPOSED, the second occurrence, the 90 day expiry to REJECTED) and Atlas's Channel 4 (archetype recurrence, origin, hardening) are model memory presented under a heading that claims computation. Channels 2, 3 and 4 for Nell and 1, 2 and 3 for Atlas genuinely are computed, which makes the framing more dangerous, not less: a reader who verifies two channels and generalises will trust the two that are prose. The concrete tell is that scout_calibrate reports notes_examined as the total note count across all signals and candidates, not notes added since the last run, so the sweep the channel is built on has no machine trace whatsoever.

challenges.claim: The ledger-line duties are enforced: 'ledger line complete' (nell-scanner.md) and check_chain's 'the ledger line names the archetypes applied and what the click queue held' (atlas-cartographer.md).
challenges.attack: For Nell the enforcement is two substring searches. Verified: a line reading 'result: applied taste rule ... queue: empty' satisfies both re.search(r'taste[- ]?(ledger|rule)') and re.search(r'(click )?queue'), with no count, no rule ids, and not one filtered candidate named, while CLAUDE.md's radar row demands 'filtered candidates listed in the ledger line' and check_radar's own docstring claims it verifies 'a taste-rules-applied count'. The check passes for the wrong reason and its failure message describes a stricter check than the code performs. For Atlas it is worse on the day it shipped: check_chain gates its ledger-content rules behind LEDGER_RULE_GATE = 2026-08-30 and today is 2026-08-29, so today < LEDGER_RULE_GATE routes both the archetype and the queue check to report() instead of fail(). The contract asserts, on 2026-08-29, that a gate enforces a rule that first becomes capable of failing on 2026-08-30. From tomorrow it checks for the presence of the word 'archetype', which a line saying 'no archetypes applied' also satisfies.

challenges.claim: The click-queue duty is discharged and visible: both files name the queue as the thing they can destroy and require the ledger line to say what it held, 'even when the answer is empty, checked first'.
challenges.attack: Nothing observes the artifact. The entire evidentiary trail for the duty is a word the agent types into a line it writes itself, after the fact. An agent that never opened the artifact and wrote 'queue: empty' passes check_radar, check_chain, both Stop hooks and CI, and its own postlude republish then deletes every click it did not see. This is the failure shape the adversary contract calls unfalsifiable: a self-report with no independent trace, guarding an irreversible action. The contracts diagnose the hazard precisely ('an entry I did not drain is not a delayed click, it is a deleted one') and then accept a self-report as proof the hazard was handled, which converts a known destructive path into a documented one. A queue block whose contents were echoed into the ledger line verbatim, or a republish that refused to run without a same-run queue read, would cost little and would make the claim capable of being false.

surviving_objection: These two files are net positive and should land. They write down duties that were nowhere before, they name their own destructive paths honestly, they record lineage instead of laundering it, and neither of them removes or weakens a single existing check. What is wrong is the register. Both files describe unenforced duties in the same voice as enforced ones, and a contract that overstates its own enforcement teaches the next reader, model or human, to stop checking. Narrow three clauses and the objection goes away. First, nell-scanner.md's 'Nothing hardens from a single note' must be restated to match data/taste.md's two-origin bar, or the two live HARDENED rules with occurrences 1 must be demoted; as written the contract and its store disagree and neither is arbitrated. Second, both files should mark which accuracy channels are computed by the calibrator and which are the agent's own writing, because scout_calibrate.py and map_calibrate.py preserve exactly the channels the contracts advertise as recomputed. Third, atlas-cartographer.md's heat boundary should say plainly that it is a prose rule, since check_chain catches only a heat block that vanished and never one that changed. The clause I would not narrow but would escalate is the zero-card radar run: no gate, no hook, and a sentinel that has never fired, which by the standard this repo applies to a dismissal with no shadow row is an unfalsifiable claim of work. If Ron adopts nothing else here, that one is worth a check_radar branch that binds on the absence of a RADAR ledger line rather than treating that absence as proof no run occurred.
